rounds.text: Om Power Transmission Ltd exhibits extraordinary compounding characteristics, boasting a 3-year compounded sales growth of 55% [E13] and an amazing trailing twelve-month sales growth of 61% [E14], which completely trounces the sector median sales growth of 5.9% [E56]. Profitability follows the exact same explosive trajectory, with 3-year profit growth at 86% [E15] and trailing twelve-month profit growth at 82% [E16], standing in stark contrast to the broader sector's median profit contraction of -4.8% [E55]. This top-and-bottom-line dominance translates into exceptional capital efficiency, highlighted by a stellar 3-year median return on equity of 33% [E17] and a recent ROCE of 42.7% [E11], comfortably outperforming the sector benchmark ROCE of 18.14% [E9]. Market pricing severely disconnects from these fundamentals, as the stock trades at a modest P/E of 14.2x [E1] while a discounted cash flow model suggests a massive intrinsic value of Rs 472 against a market price of Rs 164 [E33], leaving a staggering margin of safety of 65.3% [E34]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF model reveals that the current share price prices in a meager 3.4% earnings growth expectation [E35], ignoring the company's proven historical growth engine. Conceded: the company carries high debtors of 180 days [E46] and registered a negative operating cash flow of Rs -26 Cr in Mar 2026 [E23].

Om Power Transmission Ltd is trading at a modest P/E of 14.2x [E1], which presents a stark contrast to its exceptional operational profitability. The company boasts a multi-year profit uptrend [E51] with compounded profit growth of 86% over 3 years and 82% over the trailing twelve months [E15, E16], alongside compounded sales growth of 55% and 61% respectively [E13, E14]. This top and bottom-line expansion is supercharged by elite capital efficiency, highlighted by a 3-year median return on equity of 33% [E17] and a recent ROCE of 42.7% [E11], both vastly outperforming the broader sector benchmarks of 15.81% and 18.14% [E8, E9]. Furthermore, the intrinsic value derived from a discounted cash flow model suggests a massive margin of safety of 65.3% [E34], while the reverse DCF indicates that the current market price implies a paltry 3.4% earnings growth against a base-case assumption of 18.0% [E35]. Conceded: [E22].
